name: Tarte au Citron
description: A buttery pâte sablée shell filled with a silken, intensely sour lemon curd just set enough to slice cleanly — the tart that separates timid lemon desserts from the real thing.

name: Tarte au Citron (gluten-free)
description: A buttery pâte sablée shell filled with a silken, intensely sour lemon curd just set enough to slice cleanly — the tart that separates timid lemon desserts from the real thing. This gluten-free version uses gluten-free plain flour blend instead of plain flour.

name: Tea Eggs (Chá Yè Dàn)
description: Hard-boiled eggs cracked and simmered in a brew of black tea, soy, star anise, and cinnamon, developing a beautiful crackled marble pattern and a deeply savory, tea-smoky flavor.

ingredients.note: Strong brewed black tea (Assam or Yunnan, double strength)
Rock sugar (small piece) or white sugar
Dried mandarin peel (chen pi) or fresh orange peel

name: Tea Eggs (Chá Yè Dàn) (gluten-free)
description: Hard-boiled eggs cracked and simmered in a brew of black tea, soy, star anise, and cinnamon, developing a beautiful crackled marble pattern and a deeply savory, tea-smoky flavor. This gluten-free version uses tamari (gluten-free soy sauce) instead of dark soy sauce, tamari (gluten-free soy sauce) instead of soy sauce.

ingredients.note: Strong brewed black tea (Assam or Yunnan, double strength)
Rock sugar (small piece) or white sugar
Dried mandarin peel (chen pi) or fresh orange peel

name: Tempeh Rendang
description: Indonesian vegan rendang where slabs of fermented soybean tempeh are slowly simmered in an aromatic coconut milk paste with galangal, lemongrass, and kaffir lime until the coconut cooks dry and the tempeh is encrusted in a dark, burnished spice coating.

ingredients.note: Dried red chilies, soaked and drained

name: Tempeh Sambal (Tempe Kering)
description: Tempeh sliced thin and fried until golden and nutty, then tossed in a sambal of red chiles, shallots, lemongrass, and kecap manis that caramelizes to a lacquer in the pan — each piece of tempeh absorbing the sweet-spicy glaze while maintaining its characteristic firm, meaty bite. It is one of the great vegan preparations: deeply satisfying in a way that has nothing to do with mimicking meat.

ingredients.note: Coconut or neutral oil for frying; for frying (only some is absorbed)

name: Tempeh Sambal (Tempe Kering) (gluten-free)
description: Tempeh sliced thin and fried until golden and nutty, then tossed in a sambal of red chiles, shallots, lemongrass, and kecap manis that caramelizes to a lacquer in the pan — each piece of tempeh absorbing the sweet-spicy glaze while maintaining its characteristic firm, meaty bite. It is one of the great vegan preparations: deeply satisfying in a way that has nothing to do with mimicking meat. This gluten-free version uses gluten-free sweet soy sauce instead of kecap manis (sweet soy sauce).

ingredients.note: Coconut or neutral oil for frying; for frying (only some is absorbed)

name: Vegetable Tempura
description: Disparate vegetables coated in an ice-cold, barely-mixed batter and plunged into oil at exactly the right temperature — emerging in a gossamer-thin, shatteringly crisp shell so delicate it is nearly transparent, the vegetable's own steam driving pockets of airy lightness beneath.

ingredients.note: Mixed vegetables: sweet potato (sliced), shiitake, green beans, lotus root, red pepper
Cake flour or all-purpose flour (very cold)
Neutral oil (sesame-sunflower blend or canola) for frying; for frying (only some is absorbed)

name: Vegetable Tempura (gluten-free)
description: Disparate vegetables coated in an ice-cold, barely-mixed batter and plunged into oil at exactly the right temperature — emerging in a gossamer-thin, shatteringly crisp shell so delicate it is nearly transparent, the vegetable's own steam driving pockets of airy lightness beneath. This gluten-free version uses gluten-free plain flour blend instead of plain flour.

ingredients.note: Mixed vegetables: sweet potato (sliced), shiitake, green beans, lotus root, red pepper

name: Pad Krapow Gai (Thai Basil Chicken)
description: The dish every Thai cook makes on a Tuesday — minced chicken with holy basil, chilies, and garlic in a searing-hot wok, finished in minutes, the basil leaves wilting into dark fragrant velvet that perfumes every grain of rice beneath them.

ingredients.note: Chicken thigh, minced or coarsely ground
Thai bird's eye chilies, sliced (adjust to tolerance)
Holy basil (krapow) leaves — NOT Thai basil

name: Pad Krapow Gai (Thai Basil Chicken) (gluten-free)
description: The dish every Thai cook makes on a Tuesday — minced chicken with holy basil, chilies, and garlic in a searing-hot wok, finished in minutes, the basil leaves wilting into dark fragrant velvet that perfumes every grain of rice beneath them. This gluten-free version uses oyster sauce (gluten-free) instead of oyster sauce, tamari (gluten-free soy sauce) instead of dark soy sauce.

ingredients.note: Chicken thigh, minced or coarsely ground
Thai bird's eye chilies, sliced (adjust to tolerance)
Holy basil (krapow) leaves — NOT Thai basil

name: Thai Basil Fried Rice (Khao Pad Krapao)
description: Day-old jasmine rice blasted in a searing wok with ground pork, fish sauce, oyster sauce, and enough Thai chilies to make the kitchen uncomfortable — then buried in an avalanche of holy basil that wilts to a glossy, anise-fragrant blanket. Topped with a fried egg whose lacey crisp edges are as important as the rice itself.

ingredients.note: Ground pork (or coarsely hand-chopped pork shoulder)
Bird's eye chilies (prik kee noo), sliced or smashed (3–6 to taste)
Holy basil (bai krapao), leaves picked — Italian basil is a poor substitute

name: Thai Basil Fried Rice (Khao Pad Krapao) (gluten-free)
description: Day-old jasmine rice blasted in a searing wok with ground pork, fish sauce, gluten-free oyster sauce, and enough Thai chilies to make the kitchen uncomfortable — then buried in an avalanche of holy basil that wilts to a glossy, anise-fragrant blanket. Topped with a fried egg whose lacey crisp edges are as important as the rice itself. This gluten-free version uses oyster sauce (gluten-free) instead of oyster sauce, tamari (gluten-free soy sauce) instead of soy sauce.

ingredients.note: Ground pork (or coarsely hand-chopped pork shoulder)
Bird's eye chilies (prik kee noo), sliced or smashed (3–6 to taste)
Holy basil (bai krapao), leaves picked — Italian basil is a poor substitute

name: Pad Kra Pao
description: Ground pork stir-fried over violent heat with bird's eye chilies and Thai holy basil until the meat caramelizes at the edges and the whole dish blooms with a peppery, clove-like fragrance that holy basil alone produces — a Bangkok street-food staple that takes 8 minutes, demands ferocious heat, and rewards with an intensity that formal restaurant versions rarely match.

ingredients.note: Thai holy basil (kra pao), leaves only
Fried egg (kai dao), one per serving

name: Pad Kra Pao (gluten-free)
description: Ground pork stir-fried over violent heat with bird's eye chilies and Thai holy basil until the meat caramelizes at the edges and the whole dish blooms with a peppery, clove-like fragrance that holy basil alone produces — a Bangkok street-food staple that takes 8 minutes, demands ferocious heat, and rewards with an intensity that formal restaurant versions rarely match. This gluten-free version uses oyster sauce (gluten-free) instead of oyster sauce, tamari (gluten-free soy sauce) instead of soy sauce.

ingredients.note: Thai holy basil (kra pao), leaves only
Fried egg (kai dao), one per serving

name: Thai Fish Cakes (Tod Mun Pla)
description: Bouncy, herb-charged fish cakes kneaded until springy, fried in oil until golden — the protein energy of fish, lifted with kaffir lime leaf and fiery red curry paste.

ingredients.note: Long beans or green beans, cut into 3 mm rounds
Neutral oil, for deep-frying; for frying (only some is absorbed)

name: Thai Red Fish Curry
description: Coconut cream and red curry paste in their essential dialogue — the paste blooms in oil until the room smells like a Thai kitchen, coconut cream added in stages to build a sauce that is simultaneously rich and electric with heat.

ingredients.note: Firm white fish (snapper or barramundi, skin-on, cut into 5cm pieces)

name: Thai Larb Gai
description: Quick-cooked minced chicken tossed with toasted rice powder, lime, fish sauce, and an avalanche of fresh herbs — bright, sharp, and texturally alive.

ingredients.note: Dried chili flakes (prik bon), or to taste

name: Toasted Farro Salad with Roasted Vegetables
description: Whole farro toasted in a dry pan until nutty and golden, then simmered until pleasantly chewy — tossed warm with caramelized roasted vegetables, fresh herbs, lemon, and good olive oil in the manner of Tuscan cucina povera: simply excellent ingredients treated with respect.

ingredients.note: Water or vegetable stock; made up to 900 ml with boiling water

name: Toasted Brown rice Salad with Roasted Vegetables (gluten- & nut-free)
description: Whole brown rice toasted in a dry pan until nutty and golden, then simmered until pleasantly chewy — tossed warm with caramelized roasted vegetables, fresh herbs, lemon, and good olive oil in the manner of Tuscan cucina povera: simply excellent ingredients treated with respect. This gluten- & nut-free version uses brown rice instead of farro or freekeh, sunflower seeds instead of pine nuts.

ingredients.note: Water or vegetable stock; made up to 900 ml with boiling water
instead of Toasted pine nuts or walnuts

name: Torta Caprese
description: The legendary cake of Capri that contains not one grain of flour — just dark chocolate, whole almonds, eggs, butter, and sugar collapsed into a dense, fudgy disc that is simultaneously a brownie, a flourless chocolate cake, and something entirely its own: cracked on top, trembling within, dusted white with powdered sugar.

ingredients.note: Blanched whole almonds (or almond flour); the source also suggests a gluten option; use the first one

name: Corn tortilla Española
description: Spain's iconic egg-and-potato torta — thin potato and onion slices slow-cooked in olive oil until yielding, then bound in beaten egg and set on both sides into a golden, slightly runny disk that's Spain's answer to the omelette.

ingredients.note: Waxy potatoes (Yukon Gold or similar), peeled and sliced 3 mm thin
Yellow onion, halved and sliced 3 mm thin

name: Tournedos Rossini
description: The composer's namesake extravagance — a thick filet mignon seared to a rosy heart, set on a butter-fried crouton and crowned with a slab of seared foie gras, the whole gilded with shaved black truffle and a glossy Madeira demi-glace that pulls every luxury into one bite.

ingredients.note: Filet mignon (two 4 cm thick tournedos, ~180 g each, tied)
White bread (two crustless rounds cut to the filet's width)
Clarified butter (for the gluten-free croutons and the sear)
Veal demi-glace (or rich brown veal stock, reduced)
Black truffle (fresh, half shaved / half minced into sauce)
Cold unsalted butter (to mount the sauce)
Fleur de sel & freshly cracked black pepper

name: Tournedos Rossini (gluten-free)
description: The composer's namesake extravagance — a thick filet mignon seared to a rosy heart, set on a butter-fried gluten-free croutons and crowned with a slab of seared foie gras, the whole gilded with shaved black truffle and a glossy Madeira demi-glace that pulls every luxury into one bite. This gluten-free version uses gluten-free bread instead of crusty white bread.

ingredients.note: Filet mignon (two 4 cm thick tournedos, ~180 g each, tied)
instead of White bread (two crustless rounds cut to the filet's width)
Clarified butter (for the gluten-free croutons and the sear)
Veal demi-glace (or rich brown veal stock, reduced)
Black truffle (fresh, half shaved / half minced into sauce)
Cold unsalted butter (to mount the sauce)
Fleur de sel & freshly cracked black pepper

name: Tres Leches Cake
description: A cloud-light genoise sponge soaked until it can hold no more liquid, drowning in a trio of sweetened condensed milk, evaporated milk, and heavy cream — served cold under a billowing canopy of lightly sweetened whipped cream.

name: Tres Leches Cake (gluten-free)
description: A cloud-light genoise sponge soaked until it can hold no more liquid, drowning in a trio of sweetened condensed milk, evaporated milk, and heavy cream — served cold under a billowing canopy of lightly sweetened whipped cream. This gluten-free version uses gluten-free plain flour blend instead of plain flour.

name: Tteokbokki
description: Chewy cylindrical rice cakes simmered in a fiery, sweet gochujang sauce — the most addictive street food in Korea, simultaneously spicy, sweet, and sticky.

ingredients.note: Garae-tteok (cylinder rice cakes, fresh or refrigerated)
Eomuk (Korean fish cake sheets, cut into strips)

name: Tteokbokki (gluten-free)
description: Chewy cylindrical rice cakes simmered in a fiery, sweet gochujang sauce — the most addictive street food in Korea, simultaneously spicy, sweet, and sticky. This gluten-free version uses gluten-free gochujang instead of gochujang, tamari (gluten-free soy sauce) instead of soy sauce, no fish cake (kamaboko, eomuk).

ingredients.note: Garae-tteok (cylinder rice cakes, fresh or refrigerated)

name: Tuna Poke Bowl
description: Hawaii's gift — sashimi-grade ahi cubed and dressed in a sesame-soy marinade that deepens its flavor without erasing it, served over warm rice with cool avocado and bright radish, a dish that exists at the boundary between Japanese and Hawaiian.

ingredients.note: Sriracha or chili oil (optional for heat)

name: Tuna Poke Bowl (gluten-free)
description: Hawaii's gift — sashimi-grade ahi cubed and dressed in a sesame-soy marinade that deepens its flavor without erasing it, served over warm rice with cool avocado and bright radish, a dish that exists at the boundary between Japanese and Hawaiian. This gluten-free version uses tamari (gluten-free soy sauce) instead of soy sauce.

ingredients.note: Sriracha or chili oil (optional for heat)

name: Tuna Tataki with Ponzu
description: Sushi-grade ahi tuna briefly seared on all sides in an almost-smoking pan until a thin cooked shell forms around a fully raw, deep-red center — sliced thin, draped with ponzu and ginger, the contrast between the warm sear and the cold interior the entire point.

ingredients.note: Sushi-grade ahi (yellowfin) tuna loin, in a block
Neutral oil with high smoke point (grapeseed or avocado)
Yuzu juice or lemon juice (optional finishing acid)

name: Turkey & White Bean Green Chili
description: A pale, creamy-bodied chili of browned ground turkey and tender white beans, pepped up with roasted green chiles, cumin, and fresh lime — mellow heat, big comfort, no tomato in sight.

ingredients.note: Jalapeño, minced (seeds in for more heat)
Roasted green chiles, chopped (canned or fresh-roasted)
Great northern beans, cooked (or canned, rinsed and drained)
Chicken stock, low-sodium; made up to 1000 ml with boiling water
Cilantro, sliced scallions, and sour cream

name: Turkey-Zucchini Meatballs in Quick Marinara
description: Lean turkey meatballs kept tender and moist with grated zucchini and Parmesan, browned in a skillet and then simmered in a fast garlicky tomato sauce until they soak up its sweetness.

name: Turkey-Zucchini Meatballs in Quick Marinara (gluten-free)
description: Lean turkey meatballs kept tender and moist with grated zucchini and Parmesan, browned in a skillet and then simmered in a fast garlicky tomato sauce until they soak up its sweetness. This gluten-free version uses gluten-free breadcrumbs instead of breadcrumbs.

name: Turkish Çılbır
description: Poached eggs draped over cold garlicked yogurt and drowned in sizzling Aleppo-red butter — a 15th-century Ottoman dish that turns breakfast into theatre with its collision of cool, hot, bright, and smoky.

ingredients.note: Garlic clove, minced to a paste

name: Turkish Roasted Vegetables with Pomegranate
description: Roasted zucchini, eggplant, and red pepper dressed with pomegranate molasses and fresh herbs — caramelized edges, sweet-tart dressing, and the tang of yogurt beneath.

ingredients.note: Globe eggplant, cut into 3 cm cubes
Red bell pepper, cut into 3 cm strips

name: Vichyssoise
description: A cold French soup as pale and smooth as porcelain — leeks and potatoes gently simmered in stock, blended until silky, then enriched with cream and chilled until the flavors deepen and the texture becomes something between velvet and liquid satin.

ingredients.note: Floury potatoes (Maris Piper or russet), peeled and cubed
Chicken or vegetable stock (good quality, not too salty); made up to 350 ml with boiling water

name: Vietnamese Caramel Fish (Cá Kho Tộ)
description: Catfish braised in a Vietnamese caramel of burnished sugar and fish sauce in a clay pot until the sauce reduces to a sticky, lacquered glaze and the fish falls into sweet-salty, deeply savory flakes.

name: Thit Kho To (Vietnamese Caramel Pork)
description: Pork belly braised in a dark amber caramel, fish sauce, and fresh coconut water until the fat is translucent-soft and the meat drinks in the salty-sweet glaze — the quintessential dish of Southern Vietnamese home cooking.

name: Gluten-free bun Cha Meatballs
description: Hanoi's answer to the grill: fat-streaked pork patties charred over coal until they blister and caramelize at the edges, then plunged into a cool, sweet-sour nuoc cham that tempers the smoke and draws out the meat's depth. The char is not incidental — it is the recipe.

name: Vitello Tonnato
description: Cold, paper-thin slices of poached veal draped in a silky cream of tuna, capers, and mayonnaise — a collision of land and sea that sounds absurd until the first bite makes it make complete, inevitable sense. A Piedmontese summer classic, best served cold enough that the sauce barely trembles.

ingredients.note: Veal eye of round or topside
Capers and lemon slices for garnish

name: White Bean, Kale & Parmesan Soup
description: Creamy cannellini simmered with a Parmesan rind until the broth turns silky and savoury, then loaded with dark ribbons of lacinato kale and brightened with lemon and a snowfall of grated cheese.

ingredients.note: Extra-virgin olive oil, plus more to finish
Cannellini beans, cooked (or canned, rinsed and drained)
Vegetable stock; made up to 1500 ml with boiling water
Lacinato kale, stems removed, leaves cut into ribbons

name: Wild Mushroom Risotto
description: Carnaroli rice coaxed ladle by ladle into a mantecatura of Parmigiano and butter, laced throughout with porcini and the dark, resinous perfume of forest fungi — a dish that rewards patience with an almost liquid, wave-like consistency.

ingredients.note: Mixed wild mushrooms (porcini, chanterelle, cremini), sliced
Warm vegetable or light chicken stock; made up to 700 ml with boiling water

name: Winter Vegetable Minestrone
description: A thick, rustic tomato-flecked soup crowded with butternut squash, savoy cabbage, borlotti beans, and little pasta, simmered with a Parmesan rind and rosemary until every spoonful tastes of the whole garden in January.

ingredients.note: Extra-virgin olive oil, plus more to finish
Whole peeled tomatoes, crushed by hand, with juices
Water or vegetable stock; made up to 2000 ml with boiling water

name: Winter Vegetable Minestrone (gluten-free)
description: A thick, rustic tomato-flecked soup crowded with butternut squash, savoy cabbage, borlotti beans, and little pasta, simmered with a Parmesan rind and rosemary until every spoonful tastes of the whole garden in January. This gluten-free version uses gluten-free pasta shapes instead of dried pasta.

ingredients.note: Extra-virgin olive oil, plus more to finish
Whole peeled tomatoes, crushed by hand, with juices
Water or vegetable stock; made up to 2000 ml with boiling water
instead of Small pasta (ditalini or small shells)

name: Xiao Long Bao (小笼包)
description: Thin, pleated dumplings cradling a pork and ginger filling suspended in aspic that melts to soup during steaming — the skin is so translucent you can see the filling shift when you lift it from the bamboo, and biting too eagerly will cost you.

ingredients.note: Pork skin aspic (dong), chilled until firm; for frying (only some is absorbed)

name: Xiao Long Bao (小笼包) (gluten-free)
description: Thin, pleated dumplings cradling a pork and ginger filling suspended in aspic that melts to soup during steaming — the skin is so translucent you can see the filling shift when you lift it from the bamboo, and biting too eagerly will cost you. This gluten-free version uses gluten-free plain flour blend instead of plain flour, tamari (gluten-free soy sauce) instead of soy sauce, dry sherry instead of shaoxing rice wine.

ingredients.note: Pork skin aspic (dong), chilled until firm; for frying (only some is absorbed)

name: Yorkshire Pudding
description: The great British batter pudding — a thin, egg-rich batter poured into searingly hot dripping fat and baked until it billows into a dramatic golden crown, crisp-walled and hollow inside, the essential companion to roast beef.

ingredients.note: Beef dripping or lard (or neutral oil)

name: Yorkshire Pudding (gluten-free)
description: The great British batter pudding — a thin, egg-rich batter poured into searingly hot dripping fat and baked until it billows into a dramatic golden crown, crisp-walled and hollow inside, the essential companion to roast beef. This gluten-free version uses gluten-free plain flour blend instead of plain flour.

ingredients.note: Beef dripping or lard (or neutral oil)

name: Zabaglione
description: A warm Italian custard of just three elements — egg yolks, sugar, and Marsala wine — whisked over a bain-marie until they triple in volume and become an impossibly light, trembling foam that tastes simultaneously of sweet wine, warm custard, and something almost ethereal.

ingredients.note: Dry Marsala wine (Florio Secco or similar)
Fresh seasonal berries or peaches, for serving
